claim: Different modes of XFEL beam generation should further improve the statistics of the XFEL diffraction data and ultimately approach those of synchrotron crystallography.

evidence: This is speculation about future improvements, supported by citations.

claim: Crystallization of the Syt1–SNARE complex took 1–3 months.
source: Crystallization took 1–3 months, making the optimization of the crystals a difficult and time-consuming process.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: All crystals appeared as single plates approximately 25 × 250 × 500 μm3.
source: All crystals appeared as single plates approximately 25 × 250 × 500 μm3 and were mounted using 0.4–0.7 mm cryo-loops.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: The Syt1–SNARE complex crystallizes in two distinct crystal forms with morphologies that were indistinguishable by inspection of the crystals.
source: The Syt1–SNARE complex crystallizes in two distinct crystal forms with morphologies that were indistinguishable by inspection of the crystals.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental observations.

claim: One crystal form arose by the doubling of a single axis of the other crystal form.
source: As one of these crystal forms arose by the doubling of a single axis of the other crystal form, we term these 'long unit cell' and 'short unit cell' crystal forms, respectively (Zhou et al., 2015; Zeldin et al., 2015; Lyubimov et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental observations, supported by citations.

claim: A 30 μm XFEL beam with a pulse duration of 40 fs in SASE mode was used.
source: We used a 30 μm XFEL beam with a pulse duration of 40 fs in SASE mode.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: The centroid of the SASE energy spectrum was calculated and used for the wavelength input to post-refinement of each diffraction image.
source: We calculated the centroid of the SASE energy spectrum and used this value for the wavelength input to post-refinement of each diffraction image.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods.

claim: Each 40 fs XFEL pulse at the XPP endstation at LCLS delivers approximately 1012 photons, depositing a dose of 0.5 MGy.
source: Each 40 fs XFEL pulse at the XPP endstation at LCLS delivers approximately 1012 photons, depositing a dose of 0.5 MGy.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: A total of 148 crystals were screened, yielding 789 images with usable diffraction.
source: A total of 148 crystals were screened, yielding 789 images with usable diffraction.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental data collection.

claim: XFEL still diffraction images were simulated using the program nanoBragg.
source: XFEL still diffraction images were simulated using the program nanoBragg (http://bl831.als.lbl.gov/~jamesh/nanoBragg/) with parameters shown in Table 2.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for simulation.

claim: The simulation parameters were optimized using a brute-force grid search scored by the Pearson correlation coefficient between the simulated image and a single observed XFEL diffraction image.
source: These parameters were optimized using a brute-force grid search scored by the Pearson correlation coefficient between the simulated image and a single observed XFEL diffraction image with a high number of strong, well-resolved Bragg peaks, hand-selected from the Syt1–SNARE complex XFEL data set.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for simulation.

claim: The conventional mosaic spread was represented by 675 discrete mosaic domains distributed isotropically and randomly over a spherical cap with diameter 0.2 deg.
source: and the conventional mosaic spread (Helliwell et al., 1982) was represented by 675 discrete mosaic domains distributed isotropically and randomly over a spherical cap with diameter 0.2 deg.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for simulation, supported by a citation.

claim: The final 432 simulated XFEL diffraction images varied from each other only in crystal orientation and the beam intensity, which were randomized shot-to-shot.
source: Apart from the random number seed used to generate noise, the final 432 simulated XFEL diffraction images varied from each other only in crystal orientation and the beam intensity, which were randomized shot-to-shot.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for simulation.

claim: The experimental and the simulated XFEL diffraction images were indexed and integrated using identical procedures.
source: The experimental and the simulated XFEL diffraction images were indexed and integrated using identical procedures (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods.

claim: A hierarchical clustering algorithm was used to separate the two crystal forms found in the experimental XFEL diffraction images.
source: A hierarchical clustering algorithm (Andrews and Bernstein, 2014; Zeldin et al., 2015) was used to separate the two crystal forms found in the experimental XFEL diffraction images.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods, supported by citations.

claim: Integrated diffraction images were scaled, merged and post-refined using PRIME with improvements in scaling.
source: Integrated diffraction images were scaled, merged and post-refined using PRIME (Uervirojnangkoorn et al., 2015) with improvements in scaling as outlined below.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods, supported by a citation.

claim: Allowing a large search radius for beam position can potentially identify an incorrect beam position.
source: Secondly, allowing a large search radius can potentially identify an incorrect beam position.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data processing experience.

claim: Eight mis-indexed frames exhibited a shift of ~1.5 mm in beam position, corresponding to a shift of one lattice spacing along the long c-axis (291 Å).
source: In the case of the Syt1–SNARE complex XFEL diffraction data, eight mis-indexed frames exhibited a shift of ~1.5 mm in beam position, corresponding to a shift of one lattice spacing along the long c-axis (291 Å, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Limiting the beam search scope to a radius of 0.5 mm resulted in only two XFEL diffraction images remaining mis-indexed.
source: We therefore limited the beam search scope to a radius of 0.5 mm. Under this condition only two XFEL diffraction images remained mis-indexed (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B), and were therefore omitted from the merged diffraction data set.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The new scaling approach scales each diffraction image to the intensity distribution calculated assuming a random distribution of atoms in the unit cell, i.e., a Wilson plot.
source: Our new approach scales each diffraction image to the intensity distribution calculated assuming a random distribution of atoms in the unit cell, i.e., a Wilson plot, generated using the scattering factors of atoms with the temperature (B) factor equal to zero and the contents of the asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods.

claim: The resolution cutoff was placed where CC1/2 fell below 0.25, yielding a merged data set that was 97.4% complete to 3.5 Å resolution.
source: The resolution cutoff was placed where CC1/2 fell below 0.25, yielding a merged data set that was 97.4% complete to 3.5 Å resolution.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods and results.

claim: Post-refinement was performed in ten cycles.
source: Post-refinement was performed in ten cycles, and at the end of each cycle a new reference set was generated by applying the new scale factors and diffraction parameters to each diffraction image and re-merging the data set.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods.

claim: Although some parameters continued to change after three cycles, little change occurred in CC1/2.
source: Although some parameters continued to change after three cycles, little change occurred in CC1/2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: After scaling each diffraction image using the idealized Wilson model, the B-factor of the initial reference was 29 Å2.
source: After scaling each diffraction image using the idealized Wilson model, the B-factor of the initial reference was 29 Å2; the B-factor value changed over the next few cycles until stabilizing at 36 Å2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The B-factor value changed over the next few cycles until stabilizing at 36 Å2.
source: After scaling each diffraction image using the idealized Wilson model, the B-factor of the initial reference was 29 Å2; the B-factor value changed over the next few cycles until stabilizing at 36 Å2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The improvements in XFEL processing methods resulted in better statistics for the XFEL diffraction data set of the Syt1–SNARE complex than previously published.
source: Taken together, the improvements in XFEL processing methods resulted in better statistics for the XFEL diffraction data set of the Syt1–SNARE complex (Table 1) than previously published (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1 and comparison to the previously published data.

claim: The reprocessed data set is more complete (97.8% vs. 87.6%, respectively) than the previously published XFEL data set.
source: In particular, the reprocessed data set was is more complete (97.8% vs. 87.6%, respectively) than the previously published XFEL data set
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1 and comparison to the previously published data.

claim: The reprocessed data set has a higher multiplicity (6.1 vs. 5.0) than the previously published XFEL data set.
source: has a higher multiplicity (6.1 vs. 5.0)
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1 and comparison to the previously published data.

claim: The reprocessed data set has a better CC1/2 (94.3% vs. 92.7%) than the previously published XFEL data set.
source: and a better CC1/2 (94.3% vs. 92.7%).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1 and comparison to the previously published data.

claim: Inclusion of the negative intensities slightly improved the merging and refinement statistics.
source: Inclusion of the negative intensities slightly improved the merging and refinement statistics (Table 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Inclusion of negative intensities improved the L-test.
source: improved the L-test (Figure 4—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Inclusion of negative intensities lowered the overall atomic model R values.
source: and lowered the overall atomic model R values (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Omitting high- or low-resolution data has a small deleterious effect on the merging statistics (Rmerge and CC1/2) and the corresponding refined atomic models.
source: Omitting high- or low-resolution data has a small deleterious effect on the merging statistics (Rmerge and CC1/2) and the corresponding refined atomic models (Table 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The intensity measurements are of roughly the same quality throughout different resolutions.
source: suggesting that the intensity measurements are of roughly the same quality throughout different resolutions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of omitting high- or low-resolution data.

claim: The electron density map generated from the XFEL data set that included negative intensities yielded higher average B-factor than that generated from the reflection set without negative intensities (~100 Å2 vs. ~50 Å2 respectively).
source: The electron density map generated from the XFEL data set that included negative intensities yielded higher average B-factor than that generated from the reflection set without negative intensities (~100 Å2 vs. ~50 Å2 respectively)
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing results.

claim: The difference in B-factor had no substantial effect on the interpretability of the electron density maps.
source: but this had no substantial effect on the interpretability of the electron density maps
evidence: This is an inference based on visual inspection of the maps.

claim: The effect of excluding negative intensities on the L-test statistics was very small for the simulated XFEL data.
source: In contrast to the substantial effect of excluding negative intensities on the L-test statistics of the observed XFEL data, the effect was very small for the simulated XFEL data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The effect on merging statistics and R-values of refined atomic models for the simulated XFEL data was similarly small.
source: The effect on merging statistics and R-values of refined atomic models for the simulated XFEL data was similarly small (Table 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The much smaller fraction of negative intensities in the simulated XFEL data (4.1%) than in the observed XFEL data (15.8%) likely explains the smaller effect of excluding negative intensities.
source: likely due to the much smaller fraction of negative intensities in the simulated XFEL data (4.1%) than in the observed XFEL data (15.8%).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of negative intensity fractions.

claim: Synchrotron data were collected using the shutterless, continuous rotation method at the Northeastern Collaborative Access Team (NE-CAT) beamline at the Advanced Photon Source.
source: Synchrotron data were collected using the shutterless, continuous rotation method at the Northeastern Collaborative Access Team (NE-CAT) beamline at the Advanced Photon Source at Argonne National Lab on a Pilatus 6M detector (Dectris).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental data collection.

claim: 80 cryo-cooled crystals were screened and the best diffraction data (in the long unit cell form) were merged from three data sets collected at three different positions on a single crystal.
source: 80 cryo-cooled crystals were screened and the best diffraction data (in the long unit cell form) were merged from three data sets collected at three different positions on a single crystal using consecutive spindle angles.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental data collection.

claim: A 30 μm beam was used throughout the synchrotron experiment.
source: A 30 μm beam was used throughout the experiment.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: Each of the three synchrotron data sets contained 150 diffraction images in 0.2° frames and an exposure time of 0.2 s.
source: Each of the three data sets contained 150 diffraction images in 0.2° frames and an exposure time of 0.2 s.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental data collection.

claim: The diffraction images were indexed and integrated using XDS.
source: The diffraction images were indexed and integrated using XDS (Kabsch, 2010)
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods, supported by a citation.

claim: The diffraction images were scaled and merged using Scala.
source: and scaled and merged using Scala (Evans, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing methods, supported by a citation.

claim: The phases for the XFEL crystal structure of Syt1-SNARE complex were determined by molecular replacement with Phaser.
source: Briefly, the phases for the XFEL crystal structure of Syt1-SNARE complex were determined by molecular replacement with Phaser (McCoy, 2007)
evidence: This is a statement about the structure determination methods, supported by a citation.

claim: The rat SNARE complex (PDB ID: 1N7S), the rat Syt1 C2A domain (PDB ID: 3F04), and the rat Syt1 C2B domain (PDB ID: 1UOW) were used as search models for molecular replacement.
source: using the rat SNARE complex (PDB ID: 1N7S), the rat Syt1 C2A domain (PDB ID: 3F04), and the rat Syt1 C2B domain (PDB ID: 1UOW) as search models.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure determination methods.

claim: The structure was iteratively rebuilt and initially refined using CNS v1.3.
source: The structure was iteratively rebuilt and initially refined using CNS v1.3 (Brunger et al., 1998), with deformable elastic network (DEN) restraints (Schroder et al., 2014), restrained grouped atomic displacement parameters (ADP) and non-crystallographic symmetry (NCS) restraints
evidence: This is a statement about the structure refinement methods, supported by citations.

claim: The structure was further refined with phenix.refine using NCS restraints, secondary structure restraints, and individual ADP refinement.
source: then further refined with phenix.refine (Adams et al., 2010) using NCS restraints, secondary structure restraints, and individual ADP refinement.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure refinement methods, supported by a citation.

claim: The unit cell dimensions for refinement were set to the mean values obtained by post-refinement with PRIME.
source: The unit cell dimensions for refinement were set to the mean values obtained by post-refinement with PRIME.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure refinement methods.

claim: Re-refinement of the Syt1 – SNARE structure against the reprocessed XFEL data resulted in better atomic model Rwork / Rfree values (29.2% / 32.9% vs. 32.2% / 35.3%) than the originally published structure.
source: Re-refinement of the Syt1 – SNARE structure against the reprocessed XFEL data resulted in better atomic model Rwork / Rfree values (29.2% / 32.9% vs. 32.2% / 35.3%) than the originally published structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by data comparing the reprocessed and original structures.

claim: The phases for the synchrotron diffraction data were determined using molecular replacement and refined in the same manner as the XFEL data.
source: The phases for the synchrotron diffraction data were determined using molecular replacement and refined in the same manner as above.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure determination methods.

claim: The test set of reflections for cross-validation used for the refinement against the XFEL data was transferred to the synchrotron data refinement.
source: We transferred the test set of reflections for cross-validation that was used for the refinement against the XFEL data.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure refinement methods.

claim: The synchrotron data-derived structure yielded slightly better Rwork / Rfree values than the structure refined against the XFEL diffraction data truncated to the same resolution (4.1 Å).
source: Refined independently from the XFEL-data derived structure, the synchrotron data-derived structure yielded slightly better Rwork / Rfree values than the structure refined against the XFEL diffraction data truncated to the same resolution (4.1 Å) (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Composite omit maps were generated to reduce the potential effect of model bias.
source: Composite omit maps were generated in order to reduce the potential effect of model bias (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for map generation.

claim: The maps were generated using phenix.composite_omit_map via the Phenix GUI, employing a single cycle of Cartesian simulated annealing (starting at 5000 K) to reduce model bias, followed by minimization.
source: The maps were generated using phenix.composite_omit_map (Terwilliger et al., 2008) via the Phenix GUI (Echols et al., 2012), employing a single cycle of Cartesian simulated annealing (starting at 5000 K) to reduce model bias, followed by minimization.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for map generation, supported by citations.

claim: Bulk solvent was excluded from the omitted regions, as that option appeared to result in stronger omit map features.
source: We chose to exclude bulk solvent from the omitted regions, as that option appeared to result in stronger omit map features.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used for map generation.

source: The merged XFEL diffraction data (Table 1A) and the merged synchrotron diffraction data (Table 1B) for the Syt1–SNARE complex, along with the corresponding atomic model coordinates have been deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB IDs 5KJ7 and 5KJ8, respectively).

source: The merged simulated XFEL diffraction data (Table 1C) and corresponding atomic model coordinates are available as Source Data files.
